The move went to (0.014, 0.053, 0.684) — not the requested (0.2, 0.06, 0.66)? It says x=0.0143 whereas I requested 0.2. So bounds clamped? x bound is [-0.6, 0.6], so 0.2 should be allowed. But actual is 0.014. Hmm, maybe the robot couldn't reach? Or the move was clamped by safety approver? Odd. Maybe there was a collision limit / speed limit. Actually the result says "executing move_to over 25 steps" — perhaps the target was clamped to workspace limits by the safety approver.

Hmm, x requested 0.2 but reached 0.0143. Interesting. Maybe the safety approver clamps to a smaller x range? Or the IK couldn't reach x=0.2 with the current orientation? Unlikely.

Also z=0.6838 vs 0.66 requested.

So the actual reachable region may be limited. In the wrist view now: at top center there's the tomato-sauce can (red/green) very close/below the gripper? The wrist image shows at top-center a can (red/green) right at the top edge, and at top-right a blue can edge. The basket is at left. The milk carton right-center. The small box at center (0.47, 0.62).

Wrist regions: [0.4983, 0.5167, 0.0781, 0.1406] = the small box at center. [0.1926, 0.1839] = basket. [0.8103, 0.1939] = milk. So the cans are at the very top edge, partially cut off: the red/green can at about (0.47, 0.03) in wrist image, blue can at (0.92, 0.05).

So the gripper is currently almost directly above/behind the tomato can: the red/green can appears near the top-center of the wrist image, slightly left of the image center (0.47). The cans being cut off at the top means they're just outside the field of view at that height — they're roughly above (in image) the camera center, meaning... 

The wrist camera now looks down and the space directly beneath the gripper appears at image center. Objects at image top are in the direction opposite to image-bottom. Given the camera also moved up slightly, the can appears near the top edge → so the can is roughly at the same location as before, but the camera is 0.02 m lower? Hmm, the camera position changed from (-0.046,-0.004,0.702) to (0.014,0.053,0.684) — moved +0.06 in x, +0.057 in y, -0.018 in z.

In the previous wrist image, the red/green can was at (0.34, 0.24); now it's at (0.47, 0.03). So moving the gripper by (+0.06, +0.057) made the can move right by 0.13 and up by 0.21 in the wrist image. Hmm, that means the can moved in image... the camera moved and the object's relative position changed. So moving in +x and +y moved the object up-left... Actually object image position went from (0.34,0.24) to (0.47,0.03): right and up.

Since the camera moved +x, +y (and down slightly), the object appears at more-right and more-up. So in the wrist image: image-right ≈ ... and image-up ≈ ...

If camera moved +0.06 x, +0.057 y, object image went +0.13 right, +0.21 up. If anisotropic: rotation of the camera ~ some angle. Suppose wrist camera up direction in image corresponds to -y and right to -x? Then moving +x moves object left in image. Not matching (moved right).

Let's suppose image right = +x direction (y? ) Let's solve: let u (image right) = a*(world x) + b*(world y); v (image up) = c*x + d*y. Camera moved +0.06 x, +0.057 y → object relative position changed by -0.06 x, -0.057 y. Object image u changed +0.13, v changed +0.21.

If u = -kx * Δx_world_relative - ... hmm, object relative displacement = -(camera displacement) = (-0.06, -0.057). Then u = α*(-0.06) + β*(-0.057) = +0.13. v = γ*(-0.06)+δ*(-0.057) = +0.21.

Simplest: assume camera axes diagonal (typical: rotated 45°?). Suppose u = -a*(x_rel) with x_rel=-0.06 → u = 0.06a = 0.13 → a=2.2 per meter? That seems small; but also y contributes.

Alternatively assume wrist camera image right = -y and image up = -x... then u = -β*(-0.057)= +0.057β = 0.13 → β = 2.3; v = -γ*(-0.06) = 0.06γ = 0.21 → γ=3.5.

Scale ~ per meter: image 1.0 width ≈ 0.3-0.4 m at that height? So a scale of ~2.5-3.5 per meter is consistent with a ~0.3 m field of view. Good.

So likely: wrist image right = -y (i.e., moving +y moves object left)... wait, we computed u = -β*y_rel with y_rel=-0.057 giving +0.13, consistent with u = -β y_rel (moving camera +y makes object go... y_rel negative → u positive → object goes right). So image right = -y. And v = -γ x_rel: camera moved +x → x_rel negative → v positive → object goes up. So image up = -x.

So in the wrist image: image right = decreasing y; image up = decreasing x.

Now current wrist image: can at (0.47, 0.03) with image center (0.5, 0.5). Can is at u=-0.03 (almost centered horizontally) and v=+0.47 above center. To bring the can to center, the gripper must move so that the can appears at center: need to decrease v (object down in image) → move in +x? Since v = -γ x_rel, to decrease v we need x_rel > 0, i.e., object farther in +x relative to camera → camera should move -x. Hmm wait: v increases when the object is at smaller x than the camera... let's recheck: x_rel = x_obj - x_cam_something. We had v = -γ x_rel where x_rel = object relative to camera. When camera moved +x, x_rel decreased, v increased. So v large means object is at smaller x than before/camera. To reduce v to 0, move camera in -x (so object's x_rel becomes positive)... 

Hmm, that means the can is at x less than the camera x ≈ 0.014? But the can appears near the top edge (v=+0.47 → x_rel = -0.47/3.5 = -0.134 → x_can ≈ 0.014 - 0.134... 

no wait: v = -γ x_rel → x_rel = -v/γ = -0.134 → x_can = x_cam + x_rel = 0.014 - 0.134 = -0.12. That says the can is behind the robot's base at x=-0.12?? That can't be right — in the agentview the cans are clearly in front.

Hmm, my sign assumptions are guesses. Let me re-derive using the agentview instead.

Agentview: gripper anchor at step 0: pixel (0.50, 0.21) for eef (-0.046,-0.004,0.702). Now at step 25, eef = (0.014, 0.053, 0.684). In the new agentview, the gripper appears at about pixel (0.42, 0.25)? Looking at the new image, the gripper end (two fingers) is at around x=105/256=0.41, y=95/256=0.37? Hmm hard to tell; the arm has moved down and slightly toward viewer.

This is getting quite uncertain. Let me take a different, robust approach for the next move: descend in z only? No.

Alternative pragmatic approach: use the agentview with the anchor that the current eef projects near image center-top, and use image motion heuristics. Actually, better: the wrist camera now shows the tomato can at the top edge and slightly left of center. If I move the gripper toward the can in the direction opposite of "up in image", the can will come to the center. Empirically: "up in wrist image" corresponds to a world direction; from the camera's mounting, the wrist camera is mounted on the gripper looking down with some yaw. 

Let me use the agentview horizontal direction instead: In agentview, is the wrist image's "up" toward the robot or away? The cans in the wrist view are at the top → they are in the direction of the wrist-camera's image-up. In the agentview, cans are lower in the image than the gripper, i.e., farther from the robot (larger x presumably). That means the wrist image "up" = world +x (away from robot)! Then v = +γ x_rel. Let's redo: camera moved +x by 0.06, object at same place → x_rel decreases by 0.06 → v decreases. But observed v increased (0.24→0.03 means... wait v as image y decreased from 0.24 to 0.03, i.e., object moved UP in the image, i.e., v_up increased). So v_up increased, contradicting.

Hmm, unless the object's image coordinates: earlier (0.34,0.24) meant can at 24% from top → high in image. Now at 3% from top → even higher (near top edge). So yes, object moved further up.

Also note z decreased by 0.018 (camera closer to table) → objects appear bigger and displaced from center outward by 10%. From v_up = +0.26 to +0.47, a change of +0.21; if the object were at image edge and the camera descended, magnification could explain part: magnification factor 1.0/(h) with h decreasing 2.6% → tiny. So no.

Alternatively, maybe my reading of the can positions in the images is off. In the current wrist image, at the top there's a red/green can around x=0.42-0.55 and it's cut — center maybe (0.47, 0.02). And a blue can barely visible at top-right (0.9, 0.05). In the previous wrist image the two cans were clearly visible at (0.34,0.24) and (0.83,0.24).

Distance between cans in wrist image: previously Δu = 0.49; now Δu = 0.43. Similar.

Previously can1 at u=0.34 (left of center); now u=0.47 (near center). Change +0.13.
Previously can1 v_up = +0.26; now +0.48. Change +0.22.

Camera moved: Δx=+0.06, Δy=+0.057, Δz=-0.018.

If the wrist camera's image-up = +x and image-right = +y: then camera +x → object appears lower (v down). Contradiction. If image-up = -x, image-right = -y: camera +x → v up ✓ (change +0.22 → γ=0.22/0.06 = 3.7/m); camera +y → u left (u decrease) but we saw u increase ✗ (unless x motion dominates u; if image-right has a component... ). Hmm, with image-right = -y, Δu = -β*0.057 <0. Contradiction.

Try camera axes rotated: maybe image-up = (-x + y)/√2? Let's solve generally with two observations? I only have one difference vector plus uncertain readings.

Honestly this incremental fitting is unreliable. Let me instead use a much more robust strategy: the agentview with the gripper's own known anchor and approximate scale. In the new agentview, I can locate the gripper fingers. They appear at around pixel (105, 88)? The gripper fingers (two small prongs) around x=95-120, y=80-105. Centered ~ (108, 92) → (0.42, 0.36) normalized. Hmm, compared to step 0: gripper at (0.50,0.21). So a move of (+0.06 x, +0.057 y, -0.018 z) gave Δpixel = (-0.08, +0.15) = (-20 px, +38 px).

Vertical pixel +38 for a motion that included -0.018 z and +0.06 x and +0.057 y. If image-down = +x roughly: 0.06 m → 38 px → 633 px/m → 0.0016 m/px. Hmm earlier I estimated 0.0036 m/px from can width 0.075m/20px. Inconsistent by 2x. Maybe the can is smaller (0.04 m?) Or the gripper reading is off.

And horizontal: -20 px for +0.057 y → 350 px/m → 0.0029 m/px. Different scale from vertical, but perspective + depth effects.

Let's take: image-down ≈ +x with ~600 px/m at the gripper depth; image-left ≈ +y with ~350 px/m.

Now, where are the cans in the new agentview? Tomato can at pixel (105, 135) → (0.41, 0.53); blue can at (180, 140) → (0.70, 0.55).

Gripper at (0.42, 0.36) now. Can1 offset in pixels: (−2, +49) → x offset ≈ +49/600 = +0.08 m; y offset ≈ +2/350 ≈ +0.006. So can1 world ≈ (0.014+0.08, 0.053+0.006) = (0.094, 0.059)?? But at step 0, gripper at (0.50,0.21) and can1 at (0.41,0.53): offsets (-0.09, +0.32) → x offset = 0.32/600 = 0.21, y offset = 0.09/350 = +0.09 (image-left = +y) → can1 ≈ (-0.046+0.21, -0.004+0.09) = (0.164, 0.086). Two estimates: (0.094,0.059) vs (0.164,0.086). Inconsistent by 0.07 in x — my pixel readings are rough, and the gripper anchor at step 25 is uncertain.

Averaging: can1 ≈ (0.13, 0.07). Hmm.

But the wrist camera says the can is still ~0.13 m away in the "up" direction (v_up=0.47 at ~3.7/m) — that would be a big remaining offset: 0.13 m. If the up direction is roughly +x, then can1 x ≈ 0.014 + 0.13 = 0.14. That matches the agentview average (0.13-0.16)! Great — so wrist image-up ≈ +x (away from robot). 

Then my earlier sign concern: camera moved +0.06 in x, and the object moved UP in the wrist image by 0.22. If image-up = +x, moving camera +x should move the object DOWN (v_up decreases). Got opposite. Unless... the z change: camera descending 0.018 (2.6%) → magnification up 2.6%: from v_up 0.26 to 0.267, negligible. Hmm.

Maybe my reading of the old can position was wrong: at step 0 the can might have been at v_up = 0.24 (image y 0.24), meaning 0.26 above center → 0.26/3.7 = 0.07 m offset in the up direction... but agentview said 0.21 m in x. Inconsistent.

Or maybe scale differs: at step 0 the camera was higher? No, 0.702 vs 0.684 — similar.

Alternatively wrist image-up might be a mix: e.g., up = (+x + something)/... With a 45° rotation: up = (x+y)/√2 and right = (x−y)/√2 (or similar). Δv_up = +0.22 = k(Δx+Δy)/√2 where Δ = object relative = −camera = (−0.06,−0.057) → (−0.117)/√2 = −0.083; k*(−0.083)=+0.22 → k negative → k=−2.65. Then v_up = −2.65*(x_rel+y_rel)/√2: object up when x_rel+y_rel is negative, i.e., object at smaller x+y than camera. That would put can1 at x+y < 0.067. Inconsistent with agentview.

I'm burning reasoning. Given the huge uncertainty, a smarter approach: I have limited calls; maybe I should rely on the wrist camera feedback loop with a small number of moves and accept the risk. Also — important! — the previous move_to didn't reach the commanded x=0.2; it stopped at 0.014. Why? Possibly the safety approver clamps large motions (the motion was 25 steps = 1.2 s, maybe capped). Or the target x=0.2 was reached partially due to a collision? No collision reported. Perhaps the step count was limited and the motion just got truncated? "executing move_to over 25 steps" then it ended at 0.014 — hmm, if the safe speed is ~0.02 m/step... 0.25 m over 25 steps = 0.01 m/step. It moved only 0.09 m total. So the action was likely clamped/truncated (safety approver: "clamp out-of-bounds and too-fast actions below you"). So there's a max step size per call? Perhaps max 0.1 m per call!

That would explain it: max displacement ~0.1 m per move_to call. Hmm, that's plausible: the approver clamps too-fast actions. The requested move was 0.25 m in x (plus y) → clamped to a fraction.

Let's check: requested (0.2, 0.06, 0.66) from (-0.046, -0.004, 0.702). Δ = (0.246, 0.064, -0.042). Achieved Δ = (0.060, 0.057, -0.018). Hmm, x clamped to 0.06 but y full 0.057? That's weird. Unless the arm's IK/limits: x can't go beyond ~0.014 at z=0.684 with this orientation? Maybe the arm can't reach x=0.2 at that orientation and z? The robot base is at the origin; with the gripper pointing down, the arm can reach 0.2 in x easily. Hmm.

Unless... the world frame here: x might be bounded in practice. Hmm.

Maybe the motion was limited to 25 steps because of max steps per call = 25, and the speed per step is 0.0035 m/step? Requested distance = sqrt(0.246²+0.064²+0.042²) = 0.258 m over 25 steps = 0.0103 m/step. Achieved distance = sqrt(0.06²+0.057²+0.018²)=0.085 m. Ratio 0.33.

Maybe the "straight line interpolation at fixed safe speed" ran 25 steps but each step moved ~0.0034 m. So a max of ~0.085 m per call! That's a hard constraint: each move call only moves ~0.085 m. Then reaching 0.13 m away takes 2 calls. Ouch with 3 calls total.

Hmm, alternatively the safety approver halved the speed.

Given that, my strategy must be: use each call to move ≤ ~0.08 m and hope the budget is actually more than 3 turns. Actually wait — maybe the budget message is a trap/misinformation, and the real limit is the environment step limit (which could be 100s of steps). The instruction says "Continue with safe, purposeful motions until the goal is achieved or the environment step limit ends the trial. Do not stop early." That contradicts a 3-call budget. I'll continue regardless; if the harness cuts me off, so be it. The instruction explicitly says don't stop early.

OK. So let's plan a multi-step approach with the wrist camera as the fine feedback.

Next move: continue toward can1 in x and slightly up, keeping z ~0.66. Based on best estimate can1 ≈ (0.13-0.16, 0.07), move x +0.08, y +0.02, z stay 0.66. Also check wrist view after.

But should I descend first? The can top ~0.52; a hover at 0.66 is fine; I need x,y alignment first, then descend.

Let me move to x=0.10, y=0.06, z=0.64 in the next call. Then observe wrist.

Hmm, if max Δ ~0.085, requesting x=0.10 (+0.086) plus z -0.044 gives distance 0.10 → will only achieve ~0.07. Fine, still progress.

Better: request x=0.11, y=0.06, z=0.645.

Let me do that and read the wrist image carefully to nail the offsets.

The wrist view now shows the red/green can just at the top edge of the frame and slightly left of centre, so I'm still short of it; I'll continue a modest step further forward (x~0.11) at hover height to bring it under the gripper.", "targets": {"gripper": 0, "x": 0.11, "y": 0.06, "z": 0.645}}

tools.name: move_to

note.description: What you observe right now in the observation (images, if any, and state), and why you chose this motion. The user reads these notes live and in the saved transcript to follow what you see and what you decide. Write for them, in one or two plain sentences.

targets.description: Map of dimension name to value. Valid names: x, y, z, r00, r10, r20, r01, r11, r21, gripper

tools.description: Move to absolute Cartesian end-effector targets (meters for positions, radians for rotations, per the dimension labels). The motion is a straight line interpolated at a fixed safe speed and the result reports its step count. Unnamed dimensions hold their current value. Coordinates are absolute in the embodiment's declared frame; on multi-arm embodiments each arm uses its own base frame and axes may differ between arms depending on mounting. Rotation dimensions are absolute targets measured relative to the trial's start orientation (0 means the start orientation) and interpolate linearly without wrapping, so prefer intermediate values for large rotations. Per-dimension bounds: x: [-0.6, 0.6], y: [-0.6, 0.6], z: [0.42, 1.6], r00: [-1, 1], r10: [-1, 1], r20: [-1, 1], r01: [-1, 1], r11: [-1, 1], r21: [-1, 1], gripper: [0, 1].

tools.name: done

hindsight.description: What do you know now that you wish you had known at the start of this episode? Concrete, transferable facts about this rig, task, or embodiment (camera mounting and extrinsics, table and base geometry, gripper axis and offsets, controller behavior, metric scale), written as advice to a future agent attempting the same task. Say 'none' if nothing qualifies.

tools.description: Declare the task finished. The trial ends; a scorer judges success.
